Auromone Curve
A wristband designed to read your cortisol from sweat all day
Visit website 
Save 
 Saved 
Auromone is building the Curve, a wellness wristband designed to read cortisol, the hormone behind energy, sleep, and stress, from the trace of sweat on the wrist continuously. Most wearables estimate stress from heart rate; the Curve is designed to measure the hormone itself, so you can see your daily cortisol pattern and how training, sleep, and travel affect it. It is in development and will publish no accuracy figures until validated against a laboratory reference. It does not detect, diagnose, monitor, or manage any condition. Reserving is free, with no card and no deposit.

Space moves photos, videos, files, links, and text between any devices using a simple six-character code or lets you start a space drop zone for local file sharing with others in the same room. It encrypts data on your device and only relays sealed chunks, so the server can’t read your content. Files auto-delete in about 15 minutes. Use it on iPhone, Android, Mac, or any browser without creating an account. Features include nearby device radar, Direct Send by @username (basic email sign-up required), Quick Drop, and Spaces for live, read-only boards that update in seconds.

Morse Messenger is a private messaging service that lets you chat without sharing your phone number or email. You create a Morse ID, connect intentionally, and keep messages, media, and calls end-to-end encrypted so only participants can read or hear them. It avoids address-book uploads, public directories, and ads, and runs over Wi-Fi without a SIM card. Funded by a simple annual subscription, Morse aligns its business model with user privacy and keeps conversations secure and discreet.
